metadata.name: deactivated-elements-fixture
metadata.description: Schema fixture: an inactive node and an inactive edge. GSSK_DeactivateNode/Edge produce this state at runtime, but no example/ model is authored with it, so tests/results/serialized/ never contained an `active` key and nothing noticed that GSSK_Init accepted it without acting on it.

_covers: Node.active and Edge.active — parsed by json_active() in src/gssk.c GSSK_Init, emitted by build_topology_json. Loading this fixture and re-serialising it is what puts `"active": false` into the corpus the schema is checked against.

nodes._note: Taken out of the network, not zeroed. A node has no k, so the flag is the only thing carrying this.

edges._note: k is deliberately non-zero. An inactive edge is inactive because of the flag; if the flag were inferred from k this edge would load as live and this fixture would flow.
The converse case: k of 0 with no `active` key is an ACTIVE edge carrying nothing, and must not be read back as deactivated.
